chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Naysaburi, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Rayyan, from Yunus, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said:

I intended to enter upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so I put on my clothes and spread out a new pallium (cloak) that I was fond of. A camel squeezed me on one of the paths, so it tore from every side, and I was saddened by that.
So I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he looked at the pallium and said to me: 'What is the matter? I see you as torn.' So I informed him of the story.

So he said: 'O Umar! When you wear a new garment, say: 'There is no god except Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah,' you will be free from misfortune. And when you love something, do not mention it frequently, for that is from what crushes you. And if you have a need from a man, do not insult him from behind (in his absence), for Allah will place that in his heart.'

key_terms.طَيْلَسَان: A type of cloak or pallium worn in ancient times
key_terms.مِنْ خَلْفِهِ: From behind him (i.e., in his absence/backbiting)
key_terms.يَهُدُّكَ: Crushes you or diminishes your status/blessing

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended etiquettes and supplications when wearing new clothes according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches Umar ibn Yazeed the spiritual etiquette of wearing new garments, linking the recitation of the Shahada to protection from *al-afah* (divine affliction or the evil eye). The Imam further connects material attachment and interpersonal dynamics to spiritual well-being, advising against excessive mention of beloved things to prevent spiritual depletion and avoiding backbiting to ensure one's needs are met, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) as a means of divine favor.
